headline: QC Court Rejects Sara Duterte Bid to Remove Judge in Grave-Threats Case
seoTitle: QC Court Denies Sara Duterte Motion to Inhibit Judge | FMB News
seoDescription: Quezon City RTC Branch 98 denied Vice President Sara Duterte’s motion seeking the judge’s inhibition in her pending grave-threats case, finding no clear evidence of bias.
deck: Quezon City RTC Branch 98 denied the Vice President’s motion for inhibition, ruling that the defense had not shown clear and convincing evidence of actual bias or prejudgment.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Quezon City Regional Trial Court Branch 98 denied Vice President Sara Duterte’s motion asking the presiding judge to inhibit or voluntarily recuse herself from Duterte’s pending grave-threats cases.

In an order dated September 14, the court rejected the motion for lack of merit and said the defense had not presented clear and convincing evidence of actual bias, prejudgment or an improper connection calling the judge’s impartiality into question.
Duterte’s lawyer Paul Lawrence Lim said the Vice President would exercise available legal remedies and comply with the court’s instruction to observe the sub judice rule.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The defense had argued that the court showed partiality by directing prosecutors to submit digital evidence that was not included in the original filing.
The grave-threats case is separate from Duterte’s impeachment trial before the Senate and should not be conflated with the impeachment proceedings.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The ruling keeps the current judge on the criminal case and removes, for now, one procedural challenge that could have altered how the case proceeds.
It is not a ruling on Duterte’s guilt or innocence. The underlying criminal allegations remain for the court to resolve.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for any motion for reconsideration or other remedy from the defense, as well as the court’s next substantive hearing in the grave-threats case.
